$comment: EZiL OS managed OpenCode configuration. Installed by worker/Dockerfile at /etc/opencode/opencode.json, the Linux managed-config location OpenCode reads on every start (https://opencode.ai/docs/config/ > Managed settings); it merges on top of, and outranks, every user, project, OPENCODE_CONFIG and OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT file. The EZiL Chat extension (extensions/ezil-chat) spawns `opencode serve` on loopback with this file in force. No secrets live here: every credential is an {env:...} reference resolved at runtime from the container environment. Keys named $comment are ignored by OpenCode (verified against opencode v2.0.19).
$comment_autoupdate: The image pins the opencode binary (OPENCODE_VERSION in worker/Dockerfile) to the @opencode/client version the extension is built against; a self-update would break that contract.
$comment_share: Sessions must never be published to opencode.ai share links from a customer workspace.
$comment_small_model: Placeholder for the cheap model OpenCode uses for session titles and other lightweight work. Points at the example Azure deployment below; change it with the real deployment name. OpenCode falls back to the primary model of the turn when this model's provider is not connected.

azure.$comment: Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI. Both env values come from the container environment; without them the provider is simply not connected and the model picker stays empty. `resourceName` is the first label of https://<resourceName>.openai.azure.com/ (or .services.ai.azure.com). Every key under `models` MUST equal a DEPLOYMENT name in that resource (OpenCode addresses Azure by deployment id) — the entries below are EXAMPLES to replace with the deployments that actually exist.
